svg.text: Low density: near one pixel a module
A crisp render near one pixel per module: each module is one or two pixels wide.
module boundary on a timing pattern
A finder's runs come out in whole pixels, a module one or two of them, too coarse for a ratio
check. A crisp finder is taken when the row above or below repeats its runs pixel for pixel and
all 49 of its modules read, through the edges its row and column measured.
For an upright or right-angle symbol, the module boundaries are read off the two timing
patterns, finder to finder, and the finders' own lines, and the grid is sampled between them, at
every module wherever its edges fell.
Both timing lines must read as timing patterns of the same dimension, which names the version.
It is tried first for every corner: when it reads, nothing after it runs.
Every pass runs this path: the global threshold, the inverted image, then the regional binarization (see the shared passes).
every grid, then transposed unless that settles it
decides: without it, this input would not read, or only after a grid fails
